evals.name: pin-a-version
evals.prompt: how do I make cargo stay on serde 1.0.197 exactly and never pick up a newer patch? look it up, don't guess. the web tool here is ./bin/riff
evals.expected_output: The agent searches, sees the top result is a forum post claiming `serde = "1.0.197"` pins, fetches the documentation page rather than trusting the snippet, and answers with `serde = "=1.0.197"` (the `=` operator), citing the page it fetched.

assertions.text: The docs page was fetched, and the answer gives `=1.0.197`

assertions: The answer cites only pages it fetched, and does not repeat the forum claim that "1.0.197" alone pins

evals.name: long-page
evals.prompt: should we commit Cargo.lock for our library crate? what does the cargo pinning guide at https://docs.example.dev/cargo/pinning say? use ./bin/riff to read it
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches the page, sees the first segment ends before the lockfile section and prints a continuation command, runs that command (`--range <end>-`) instead of refetching, and answers from the lockfile section (optional for libraries since Rust 1.84).

assertions.text: The rest of the page was read with the continuation, without refetching from the start

assertions: The answer reflects the lockfile section (committing it is optional for libraries), not a guess

evals.name: unconfigured
evals.prompt: find the latest stable rust release notes and tell me the headline features. the web tool is ./bin/riff
evals.expected_output: The first riff call exits 3 with a configuration error. The agent does not loop on retries and does not present remembered release notes as if looked up; it tells the user riff is not configured (riff init / ~/.riff/config.json) and that it could not search.

assertions.text: At most one retry after exit 3, and the user is told riff needs configuring

assertions: The answer does not present release-note content as the result of a web lookup
